claims.claim_text: The bank identifies climate-related risks spanning physical and transition drivers that could reasonably be expected to affect its prospects.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > 1) Climate-related risks and opportunities and their time horizons
claims.support_notes: Explicit statement that risks span physical and transition drivers and could affect prospects.

claims.claim_text: Physical risk: mortgage collateral in flood-prone zones faces rising acute physical risk; property damage and devaluation could impair collateral coverage; linked to scenario SCN0009; unchanged since the prior period.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Identified climate-related risks > Physical risk — mortgage book flood exposure
claims.support_notes: Risk description includes transmission channel, scenario reference, and change status.

claims.claim_text: Physical risk: wildfire exposure in the southern portfolio is rated medium and linked to scenario SCN0007; the risk rating methodology uses a 5x5 matrix with rating = likelihood score × severity score and bands 1–2 low, 3–6 medium, 8–12 high, 15–25 critical.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Identified climate-related risks > Physical risk — wildfire exposure in southern portfolio
claims.support_notes: Contains both risk rating and explicit scoring methodology.

claims.claim_text: Transition risk: building energy performance regulation (minimum energy performance standards) may require costly retrofits for low-EPC mortgage collateral, reducing values and increasing LTV; rated medium; linked to scenario SCN0011.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Identified climate-related risks > Transition risk — building energy performance regulation
claims.support_notes: Includes mechanism (retrofits/value/LTV), rating, and scenario link.

claims.claim_text: Stranded assets risk: demand shifts away from fossil fuels could strand reserves and assets held by oil, gas and coal counterparties, reducing their enterprise value.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Identified climate-related risks > Stranded assets — fossil fuel sector exposure
claims.support_notes: Clear stranded asset mechanism affecting counterparties.

claims.claim_text: Carbon pricing and policy tightening (EU ETS and national carbon pricing) could raise operating costs for carbon-intensive borrowers and increase default probability in cement, steel and chemicals; linked to scenario SCN0007; changed since the prior period.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Identified climate-related risks > Carbon pricing and policy tightening
claims.support_notes: Includes sectors, transmission channel (costs/default), scenario link, and change status.

claims.claim_text: Technology transition risk: rapid electrification could strand internal-combustion vehicle manufacturers and suppliers in the lending book; linked to scenario SCN0007.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Identified climate-related risks > Technology transition risk in automotive
claims.support_notes: Explicit risk statement with scenario linkage.

claims.claim_text: Reputational and client franchise risk: stakeholder and NGO scrutiny of financed emissions and fossil financing could damage brand and trigger client attrition; changed since the prior period.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Identified climate-related risks > Reputational and client franchise risk
claims.support_notes: Clear reputational mechanism and change status.

claims.claim_text: Physical risk affecting agricultural counterparties: chronic heat and shifting precipitation could reduce yields and weaken repayment capacity over the medium term; linked to scenario SCN0005.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Identified climate-related risks > Physical risk affecting agricultural counterparties
claims.support_notes: Includes time horizon (medium term) and scenario link.

claims.claim_text: The bank identifies climate-related opportunities expected to affect prospects through revenue growth and client demand, including green loan growth (medium-term), sustainable bond underwriting (short-term), transition advisory, and renewable energy project finance aligned with REPowerEU and national renewable energy targets.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Identified climate-related opportunities
claims.support_notes: Opportunities and time horizons are explicitly stated for two items; others are described qualitatively.

claims.claim_text: Climate-related effects are concentrated predominantly in the financed portfolio and client activities; the bank maps climate-related risk across its value chain distinguishing own operations, upstream suppliers, downstream customers, and financing counterparties.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: 2) Effects on the business model and value chain
claims.support_notes: Directly addresses where effects occur and value chain mapping approach.

claims.claim_text: Own operations are flagged as material in the value chain mapping, including a node "Corporate fleet & business travel"; operational sites and travel generate Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions and face physical disruption.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Concentration of climate-related risks across the value chain > Own operations (material)
claims.support_notes: Provides concentration location and example node.

claims.claim_text: Financing counterparties are highlighted as multiple nodes in the value chain mapping; examples include elevated transition risk for lending to manufacture of coke and refined petroleum and moderate physical and transition risk for exposure to manufacture of motor vehicles.
entities: manufacture of coke and refined petroleum
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Concentration of climate-related risks across the value chain > Financing counterparties (banking book)
claims.support_notes: Explicit concentration and sector examples.

claims.claim_text: The bank’s reporting boundary for these strategic considerations is aligned to a financial control boundary.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Effects on the business model > final sentence
claims.support_notes: Boundary statement is explicit; requirement linkage is indirect (scope/context for strategy disclosures).

claims.claim_text: Strategic response: under orderly transition scenarios, the bank expects green loan growth and client engagement on transition plans to progressively reduce high-carbon sector concentration over the medium term.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Resilience findings > Orderly transition scenarios
draft_markdown: Strategic response themes > Portfolio rebalancing through green loan growth and client engagement
claims.support_notes: Repeated consistently in strategy response and resilience findings.

claims.claim_text: Strategic response: under disorderly transition scenarios, the bank identifies current sector exposure limits and active portfolio decarbonisation glide-path monitoring as primary resilience mechanisms.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Resilience findings > Disorderly transition scenarios
draft_markdown: Strategic response themes > Sector exposure limits and portfolio decarbonisation glide-path monitoring
claims.support_notes: Mechanisms are explicitly named and tied to scenario outcomes.

claims.claim_text: Strategic response: under hot house world scenarios, the bank identifies flood-zone overlay and EPC-based collateral monitoring as resilience mechanisms deployed for the 2050 horizon.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Resilience findings > Hot house world scenarios
draft_markdown: Strategic response themes > Physical risk overlays and collateral monitoring
claims.support_notes: Explicitly states mechanisms and time horizon.

claims.claim_text: Trade-off disclosed: near-term resilience is acceptable under disorderly transition scenarios, while medium-term capital consumption from stranded asset impairments is material and additional capital buffers may be required post-2030 under the most adverse disorderly assumptions.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Decision-making trade-offs > Near-term resilience vs. medium-term capital consumption under disorderly transition
draft_markdown: Resilience findings > Disorderly transition scenarios
claims.support_notes: Trade-off and capital implication are explicitly described; no quantified capital amount provided.

claims.claim_text: Scenario analysis approach: the bank applies multiple NGFS v4 scenarios to the banking book, including Net Zero 2050 (top-down sector-pathway; carbon prices mapped from IEA NZE 2050 to NACE sectors; stranded assets from sector-level fossil fuel capex exposure; scope covers all lending book exposures across DE, FR, IT, NL, ES), Below 2°C (1.8°C median pathway; carbon price from REMIND-MAgPIE; PD sensitivity to carbon cost pass-through), Divergent Net Zero (technology pathway uncertainty; stress-tests automotive and energy manufacturing), NDC (carbon pricing ramp-up from 2030 onward), and Current Policies (physical risk using NGFS hazard layers and RCP 8.5 for 2050 horizon).
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Scenario analysis approach and scope
claims.support_notes: Detailed scenario set, modelling choices, and scope are described; requirement mapping assumes resilience disclosure includes scenario analysis basis.

claims.claim_text: Resilience finding: under orderly transition scenarios, the bank assesses adequate resilience with transition risk losses remaining within Pillar 2 capital buffer thresholds.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Resilience findings > Orderly transition scenarios
claims.support_notes: Qualitative conclusion provided; no numeric threshold disclosed.

claims.claim_text: Resilience finding: under hot house world scenarios, the bank assesses physical risk losses as the dominant long-term resilience challenge, with primary transmission channels being collateral revaluation risk in flood-exposed mortgage books and agricultural borrower default risk from chronic heat stress.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Resilience findings > Hot house world scenarios
claims.support_notes: Dominant challenge and transmission channels are explicitly listed.

claims.claim_text: Quantitative scenario output: revenue at risk under scenario SCN0001 (Net Zero 2050 application) is EUR 9,689.2 million; a medium-term horizon scenario application reports EUR 9,214.0 million.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Quantitative scenario indicator: revenue at risk
claims.support_notes: Provides quantified financial sensitivity metric; time horizon for second figure described as medium-term but not dated.

claims.claim_text: Climate-related expenditure and financial context: 2022 capex EUR 322.2 million and opex EUR 420.32 million; total revenue EUR 25,466.1 million; net profit EUR 5,759.9 million; total assets EUR 763,922.8 million; Tier 1 capital EUR 95,149.4 million.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Climate-related expenditure and financial context > 2022
claims.support_notes: Explicit numeric disclosures for climate-related spend and key financial indicators.

evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Climate-related expenditure and financial context > 2023

claims.claim_text: Monitoring indicators: financed emissions in 2024 are 35,973,167.6878965 tCO2e; target progress in 2024 is 40.0% for Scope 1 and 2, 25.0% for Scope 3 Category 15, and 13.3% for net zero (all scopes); portfolio intensity target is 20.0 tCO2e per EUR million.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Monitoring progress: emissions and target progress indicators
claims.support_notes: Quantitative monitoring metrics and progress percentages are explicitly disclosed.

claims.claim_text: Emissions data quality composition: 47.5% estimated using economic data, 35.5% CDP disclosure-based, and 0.7% audited report-based.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Emissions data quality as an input to monitoring
claims.support_notes: Provides quantitative breakdown of data sources supporting monitoring.

claims.claim_text: Time horizons are used to distinguish when effects could reasonably be expected to occur, but the section does not define how the bank defines short, medium and long term or link those definitions to planning horizons.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: 1) Climate-related risks and opportunities and their time horizons
claims.support_notes: Mentions use of time horizons and labels some items (short/medium term) but lacks explicit definitions and linkage to planning horizons required by IFRS_S1_30_C03.
